inline.s: Praise of Chan Master Guifeng

To win a marquisate ten thousand li away, he cast aside his brush and took it up. Our master cast aside one thing and passed straight out of birth and death. Together they roam the sea of nature; his is the seal of a true son. He entered the gate of the dharma-realm, and so is called the Second Sage.
Praise of National Master Fazhao

The Great Being Mañjuśrī, whom he longed to see but once, therefore appeared beforehand in his alms bowl as the golden realm. When he came to the gate it was as if returning to a place long known. Pointing straight to the Land of Ultimate Bliss — that is where he took refuge.
Praise of Tripitaka Master Xuanzang

The great teaching flowed east, yet its dharma was not yet widespread. Then came a true arhat who gave up his life to go and fetch it. The light of prajñā streamed forth, and the school of Dharma-Characteristics opened wide. A boat upon the sea of suffering, bestowing benefit without end.
Praise of Master Kuiji

The profound doctrine of consciousness-only, its meaning deep and dark: only the master made it shine, like the sun in the sky. Surely he came from Tuṣita, having received the charge from Maitreya beforehand. Had he not come from there, who could know its secret?
Praise of Vinaya Master Daoxuan

The Tathāgata set up the teaching with the three trainings as its master. What samādhi and wisdom bring forth has the precepts as its base. When the great dharma flowed east, this teaching had not yet shone; then the master of Nanshan arose and roused its guiding line at once.
Praise of Chan Master Yixing

The exoteric and esoteric schools, the lore of omen and calendar: once the Great Expansion was complete, yin and yang fell into measure. Worldly and world-transcending dharmas alike he mastered and refined. The conduct of the fifth ground was seen in the master.
Praise of Chan Master Nanyue Huairang

His spirit soared to heaven, his mind empty beyond measure. He scooped up the waters of Caoxi and raised up waves and billows. The colt that lay asleep he roused with a single brick; then it kicked and trampled where it would, and all it touched fell dead.
Praise of Chan Master Qingyuan Xingsi

Naturally noble, he fell into no grades or stages. One word struck the mark, like a bee finding honey. From the single stream of Caoxi branch split and channel spread; from then on his heirs rolled on like thunder and lightning.
Praise of Master Wuxiang of Yongjia

His golden staff stood alone as a mark, a living dragon and a leaping tiger. Had it not been for old Lu, he would have been slighted again and again. He understood before a word was spoken and set out after a single night. Yet even such transcendence leaves him still a son and heir.
Praise of Chan Master Daoyi of Xijiang

The colt was a dragon: he walked like an ox and glared like a tiger. One hundred and thirty men — one stamp of the foot. The dharma flowed to the West River; a hundred streams poured east. A single drop spread everywhere and slaked the parched and barren.
Praise of Chan Master Shitou Xiqian

The barbarian's buddha-nature had its cause from the first. At a single word to go and reflect, he straightway got the truth. He sat perched on a rock, and that road is very slippery; even one who can walk it takes a tumble.
Praise of Chan Master Dazhu Huihai of Yuezhou

Holding the treasury himself, he yet sought it from another. One word pointed it out, and in response and function he was free. Yuezhou had a great pearl, round and bright, clear through and through; it shines wherever it turns and never falls into the old ruts.
Praise of Chan Master Tianhuang Daowu

He did not dwell on that shore — from where then did he come? One meeting with Shitou and the gate flew open. With this he showed people, prizing only that they know what they have. Picking it up upside down, he was like a man juggling balls.
Praise of Chan Master Weishan Lingyou of Tanzhou

Baizhang stood like a wall, and those who came gazed up from the cliff. Only the master went straight in; poking the fire, his mind opened. He took birth as a water buffalo and moved among the different kind; Yangshan saw through him — the family name of father and son.
Praise of Chan Master Niaoke Daolin of Hangzhou

He came riding the sunlight and dwelt according to his own nature. So when he first appeared, his awakening was naturally wondrous. He nested in a tall pine; people called it perilous, but he only watched others and never checked himself.
Praise of Chan Master Huangbo Xiyun of Hongzhou

Beneath Mount Daxiong there was a great beast; one roar and all who heard were deafened. His pivot was the swift thunder, his eye the flashing lightning. The style of the coming from the West grew perilous indeed from him on.
Praise of Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Zhenzhou

A lion of Huangbo, barely showing claw and fang. His pivot with Dayu was like an eagle seizing a hare. Three blows under the ribs, one slap on the cheek — he merely chanced to cross its edge; it was no crude rashness.
Praise of Chan Master Dongshan Liangjia Wuben of Duanzhou

His original face — one touch and it was seen. That insentient things expound the dharma still seemed to fall short. After meeting Yunyan he overturned the old nest; crossing the water he saw his shadow, and only then was he clear through.
Praise of Chan Master Caoshan Benji of Fuzhou

His capacity overleapt the norm and left no trace of name. With an eye beyond the ordinary, one glance and he knew. The five ranks, empty and dark; the essential teaching, fine and close-woven. Therefore to this day it is still black as lacquer.
Praise of Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun of Fuzhou

What is familiar is hard to forget — the habit of vegetables and bamboo shoots. Bell, chanting, and the sound of sutras: hearing them, his heart grew drunk. The master's staff was like a dragon, his friend's mouth like iron; hence his emergence in this life was naturally transcendent.
Praise of Chan Master Yunmen

No sooner had he met Muzhou than the door was shut and he was pushed out; pressing in, he was squeezed, and his leg was snapped off. From that turning he covered heaven and covered earth. Before he ever met Xuefeng, his mind had already chimed.
Praise of Chan Master Fayan

All is ready-made, with no hesitation at all. Amid the ten thousand forms he stands out boldly alone. One flavor, an even mind — it is right before the eyes. The moment thought stirs, one falls to the second.
Praise of Chan Master Shoushan Shengnian of Ruzhou

The seven scrolls of the Lotus Sutra he had long upheld; at one word he let them go and knew at once what he had always had. The teaching that is no teaching — bring it up and it appears. He shook his sleeve and went his way: what briskness, what ease.
Praise of Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai of Yuezhou

Compassionate by nature, he came to settle an old debt. Seeing a fish, he at once let it go. Once out of the dusty net, he straightway climbed the ground of awakening. The carrying pole snapped, the bucket fell away, and empty space shattered.
Praise of Chan Master Shishuang Chuyuan Ciming of Tanzhou

The Western River's counter-pivot none who saw could recognize. He himself had his mouth covered and lost his nostrils. His pivot shot out swift, breaking free beyond all tether. The clear-eyed praised him: a true lion's cub.
Praise of Chan Master Huanglong Huinan of Longxing Prefecture

A lion of the Western River, the family style of father and son. Gripping the Tai’e sword point-down, who dared face its edge? The master crossed it once, and the feelings of sage and ordinary were spent. In his room, three barriers; he raised the true command in full.
Praise of Chan Master Yangqi Fanghui of Yuanzhou

He shouldered the great dharma and held the monastery's net together. Meeting on a narrow road, one word revealed the mind. In later days his heirs filled the whole world: the source far, the stream long; the roots deep, the branches great.
Praise of Chan Master Shouduan of Baiyun Monastery, Shuzhou

Long he held a bright pearl, hoarding it as rare goods. When at last he met an expert, one laugh and it dropped. Seeing through the place of that laugh, he too fell over laughing. Whatever he picks up at random is nothing but treasure.
Praise of Chan Master Wuzu Fayan of Qizhou

He set out ill-starred and at once ran into a plank-carrier. Meeting anyone he questioned them, but it only served to screen his eyes. Luckily he met an expert, and one blow of the mallet broke it open. Turning his head back, he knew his words had fallen flat.
Praise of Chan Master Zhijue Yanshou of Huiri Yongming, Hangzhou

Riding the power of great vows, he appeared as an auspicious sign of dharma. The gate of dhāraṇī opened, and all practices were complete. He hung up the mirror of the one mind, brightly lighting all things. The Buddha-sun at midheaven leaves no darkness unlit.
Praise of Chan Master Gaofeng of Tianmu

The peril of Snow Cliff, a wall standing ten thousand fathoms — only the master climbed it and found the shortcut. The peril of the Death Pass exceeds the cliff itself; so those who gaze at it feel they are climbing to heaven.
Praise of Chan Master Zhongfeng of Tianmu
In the lair of Tianmu, a true lion's cub: barely showing claw and fang, and a hundred beasts fled. Lone peak, austere; dharma ocean, vast. Therefore our master is called king among monks.

He perched on the high peak of Tianmu and pierced the iron wall in empty space. He shattered the heavy barriers of buddhas and patriarchs and made light of the learning of a dust-mote world. He showed a body and mind like an illusion and displayed the samādhi-power of the nāga. He smashed the nest of living beings' birth and death — meet him though you may, there is nowhere to find him.
Praise of Chan Master Qianyan

He asked where the Buddha was; he sought but did not see. A rat upset the dish, and suddenly it appeared. He leapt up like space itself, answering sound with echo. Had it not been for this turn, he would have nearly drowned in idle thought.
Praise of Chan Master Foyin

The habit of letters leaked out from birth; with a mouth askew he spoke of Chan and never fell into old ruts. He painted his smiling face beforehand, none knows why; laughing aloud, he passed away. That very thing is it.
Praise of Chan Master Wuzhun of Jingshan

One word struck the mark, and the ten directions were clear through. From his tongue-root thunder ran; monks gathered like clouds. Twice he entered the inner court and guided the ten-thousand-chariot sovereign. He borrowed no other's power but relied wholly on the true command.
Praise of Chan Master Jizhao Yuanming

As the ways of the world rose together, the true man answered the times. Clouds and dragons, wind and tigers — none could hold him back. True gold comes out of the ore; an ancient mirror gives forth light. Once the bright essence is released, its shining function has no fixed direction.
Praise of Chan Master Baiyun Jue

He sat on White Cloud Peak with a tongue of crashing thunder. The sea of nature heaved its waves; the sky of meaning arrayed its stars. Dragons and spirits ran at his bidding, and demon hordes melted away unseen. One drop of coolness broke the fever of the miasmic air. A fine master indeed, of the fullest measure — were it not for that beard covering his mouth, people would surely take him for Kāśyapa on Vulture Peak.
Praise of the Vajra Stupa

I bow to the Vajra Banner, bright gathered light of prajñā, the mind of every living being, and so the mother of all buddhas. It enters every dust-mote and can do the work of benefit. How good, this man of wondrous wisdom, who from a subtle, fine-grained thought raised up this banner most supreme, like a lotus treasury. The banner stands upon a dust-mote; in one mote a single word is written. Mote within mote, worlds complete; word within word, light appears. And in this single banner, every mote assembled, the full conditions of prajñā are met, neither added nor diminished. Know then that the minds of living beings are each and all complete. I look upon this body of mine and find it no different from this peerless banner. The subtle mind of daily use rests wholly on the power of prajñā. If for a single thought one gazes in reverence, all is complete; thought after thought never apart from mind, and every merit is perfected.
Praise of the Painting of the Three Teachings

One yet three: a newborn child dressed in a flowered cloth coat. Three yet one: a tuneless tune blown on a holeless flute. He lies without a blush and hides his heart black as lacquer. Do not say his heart and soul are of two kinds; who can see through the true message? A heart full of matters it is hard to tell — the cuckoo's blood dyes the spring hills wet.
Praise of Emperor Wenchang

The essence of creation, blazing forth as pattern and letter, shining through the long night while sun and moon take turns to give light. Nothing but your utmost; silent, you are still. When one knocks, it sounds like a bamboo flute — deep, deep, never exhausted, like a valley that yet seems full. The Lord comes forth at the trigram Zhen: this is what is called utmost spirit.
Praise of Laozi Riding the Ox
The purple vapor came from the east; the black ox passed away to the west. He was not looking for anyone — what was it all for?
Praise of Laozi Passing the Pass

His mind dwelt in the most ancient; his Way turned from the shallow world. He shone without dazzling, was empty without bending. He reached emptiness and kept stillness, thought little and desired little; calm and tranquil, he gladdened the spirit, utterly without possessions. While the rival lords struggled and raced one another, while the tripods boiled in the Central Plain, he turned his longings toward the West. No sooner had he mounted the black ox than the purple vapor rose. The Keeper of the Pass knew beforehand that the True Man was coming; he bowed to his command and gazed up in reverence, begging him to unlock the hidden mystery. He left behind five thousand words: the Way complete, the virtue full. He did not place himself before things, nor begin any calamity. Humble in the Way, without self; knowing contentment, knowing when to stop. He blended with the world and softened his light, and none could take his measure. Therefore he was called like a dragon, and served as Keeper of the Archives.
Praise of Confucius

Teacher of a hundred kings, mandate of a thousand sages, the moral order of all ages, the true nature of every living being. He bore it all on his single strength, leaving nothing over. Had our master not been a man beyond measure, who could keep human relations upright forever?
Praise of Pengzu

His complexion like an infant's, his breath like a babe's; he drank the wind and supped on dew, and dined on cloud. Once in three thousand years the flat peach ripens — he was already a boy, and still he plucked the flowers.
Praise of Lü Chunyang

The universe within his hand, the ten thousand transformations born of his body. He received the purest essence of the three powers and won the fine purity of the two breaths. Bearing the green serpent sword, he sported without hindrance; meeting Huanglong, his wondrous awakening was made true. At dawn he roamed the isle of Penglai; at dusk he lodged on Kunlun. His years are as heaven and earth, his virtue like the spring sun. This is what is called a sage among men — or rather, a spirit among immortals.
Praise of the Marquis of Hanshou

Austere, as if alive; bright, as if present. A loyal heart glowing alone, a bearing majestic and grand. Spirit on his face, a heap of rock in his breast. Everywhere he meets people he loves to show himself — most likely his hero's debt is still unpaid.
Praise of the Half-Portrait of Master Yufeng of Mount Qingliang

A half-round moon, a single drift of cloud; snow grown old, ice dried up, water clear, sand shallow. People say he is a son of the first patriarch; I say he is Mañjuśrī's companion. Eighty years of ascetic practice without end, a hundred thousand kalpas fulfilled in a single thought. Who knows from which life came the old foe who came to this world to repay a former debt? Late he got a son neither lay nor monk, who put on a face neither true nor false. Yi! Today we meet again with a laugh, and wait only for the first assembly beneath the Dragon-Flower Tree.
Praise of Master Baofeng

True yet not true; no mark, and yet no lack of marks. Like color within a pearl, like an image in a mirror. He wandered the whole trichiliocosm and left no trace; the ten directions fell away with no obstruction. To strike the iron ox of Shaanfu, he snapped the bamboo staff of Qiongzhou. In the north the mountains are cold and snow is flying; in the south the earth is warm and flowers first open. Meeting you, he will not reveal the whole pivot, but says only that both is and is not are slander. Ask where that elusive master whom no one can lay hold of may be — people say he is Master Baofeng before the Son of Heaven's gate.
Praise of Master Zibai

The net of the dharma-realm was torn and its cords no longer drawn taut; then the master was born and by his strength pulled its main line up. He sat in the lion's den and felled the sandalwood tree. Before his spring was spent, claw and fang already showed. He beat the drum smeared with poison and poured out the sweet-dew draft; those who drank were drunk, those who heard went mad. In the stillness of extinction, his tongue crashed like thunder; rushing storm and coiling lightning — all it touched lost their souls. With the mind of the great earth, with bones firm as diamond, sinew in his eyes and nothing in his breast. Linji did not die, Huangbo still lives. Who knew the master would not accept their names? Broad and open his stride, keeping no rule or track; he turned and flung himself over Mount Sumeru and shattered the land of no-birth with one blow of his fist.

He sits alone on the lonely peak, his robe open to the hidden sea. A shout wakes the fish and dragons; ghosts and monsters melt away unseen. Propped on his ruyi staff, both eyes empty; the worlds of the ten directions have no cover. Do not say the spring wind is the same everywhere: ice is dried and snow grown old, yet the cold cliff remains.

An eye that settles heaven and earth, like a precious mirror hung on high: whoever stands before it, fair or foul cannot hide. Grip the Tai’e sword point-down and give it to others without grudging. Māra and the outsiders who cross it lose body and life. A fist struck by no hand — the fist is not in the hand; speech understood with no tongue — the words are not in the mouth. Brows and beard slightly shown, his form seems to exist; but knock at what is within, and he cannot split it open himself.

His face like the moon, his heart like iron; short hair and long beard, his bearing wholly apart. One clench of the fist and both eyes are empty; the spine straightens and all conditions cease. He smashes the diamond ring and perfects the extinction of sweet dew. The worlds of the ten directions have no barrier; a single ray of spirit-light is never idle through. Meeting him suddenly, the nose aches — there is a pain in the heart that is hard to tell.

Blood and sweat over his whole body, like a lion bursting its bonds. He snaps the root of affection and lays down the heavy burden. Without, he seems walled and guarded; within, he has no cliff or bank. Two eyes wide open — and there is only this fellow to see.
Praise of Master Yunqi

He came riding the power of his vows and dwelt in this world of endurance. He opened the gate of the Pure Land and settled the debt of compassion. He raised the banner of light and kept the diamond precepts. For more than eighty years, half of it spent in benefiting beings; at the end he left with only emptiness, without hindrance. If you would know the mind with which our master dwelt in the world, this is what is called Avalokiteśvara.

I look upon the master: lively in every part; through all his pores the light shines clear. His face and eyes are not seen — how then portray them? Even if one paints him well, in the end one does not hit it. He sits calm as space and speaks the dharma like the wind. To chase the wind and snatch at shadows, one cannot find their track. Hearing wind in the air, seeing shadows in water — how many foolish people sit dozing with their eyes open.

He dwells in emptiness and lives by wisdom; he enters the minds of living beings and practices Samantabhadra's conduct. Whether scaled or feathered, all alike enter the one equal dharma-nature: one flavor of compassion, fully pure. If you ask what dharma-gate our master used, the samādhi here is clearly without contention.
His mind like the moon in the sky, his form like an image in a mirror: this is our master through forty years, a true model of accord with living beings.

His countenance still, his mind close-held; no inside or outside, no going out or coming in. A hundred thousand samādhis are flowers in the eye; all gates of practice are bird-tracks in the sky. If you do not believe he divides his body among the ten thousand forms, the fool goes looking for him at the tip of a hair. Yi!
Praise of the Circle Portrait of Master Wuming

Long have I heard the name of Wuming, but never seen Wuming's face. Then a great mountain stood out, and we met across a thousand li. His livelihood was in his hoe; he taught the dharma like running lightning. He draws the stringless bow and is used to the arrows of Shigong; he only wants to shoot a man, and the man flees at the twang. But when he strikes a stubborn rock, head and feather both sink in. He flings out the iron lump, and all who see it are left without a reckoning. This is our master's old skin of a face: look at it, and you may only understand it before a word is spoken. If you ask about the upward pivot in broad daylight, cloud-wrapped mountains fill the eye and are hard to tell apart.
Praise of Master Wubian

The sea of lands is boundless, and not one dust-mote stands. Wherever his heel lands, conditions gather. A monastery that follows him about; tea and rice as plain as home; all who come are filled, and he does as he pleases. One stamp at the Wu River, and the dharma-pole is set up; dragons and elephants come galloping with no turning back. Clouds rise on the Twin Paths; the single transmission's moon is bright. Who is it that shouts aloud? The master answers as its echo. At the tip of a single hair he manifests the jewel-king's realm. Through eighty-eight generations none has closed the case. The whole pivot of the Way's fortune depended on the master's one flick. Half a nostril — who ever touched it?
Praise of Master Kongyin of Mount Qingliang

In the golden realm he ever followed the great assembly; only the master led the disciples and quietly wielded his great function. The five peaks stand high; as he walked in practice he looked and paused. Through ten thousand gorges the wind howled, and the sound of dharma spread everywhere. He roamed the sea of extinction and sat in the grove of sundry flowers, sporting like a lion, glancing, yawning, stretching often. His fame reached the ninefold court; his pure wind cleared the world. The ten directions took refuge in him, like the sea drawing in water. His form did not mirror his mind; the true does not mix with the common. One sees only his skin — who has gotten his bones? When the dharma banner toppled and the teaching net was no longer tight, the master pulled up its main cord like silk woven in heaven. The wise man has gone; a thousand years of stillness. Heaven truly gave him birth, and his bearing is unchanged. A thousand feet of cold cliff, ten thousand years of ice-cave: I sit before him, the master treads behind. I am driven by karma, he sustains by vow; heat and cold differ, but in this there is no shifting. When the kalpa-fire blazes, ice dries and snow grows old; once the phantom film is removed, the sky-flower is finished too. The floating clouds scatter and the blue sky is high; one round bright moon hangs clear in the void. Let me ask the man in the Vajra Cave: before and after, three and three — how many does that make?
Another Half-Body Portrait

This old fellow — where does he come from? No one knows why his face is covered with dust. A thousand feet of ice and snow could not freeze him to death; half of him remains, setting everyone guessing. How strange: the bell beneath the lion's neck — he tied it himself and untied it himself. Truly marvelous!
Praise of Master Shaojue

He takes the dharma as his body and wisdom as his life; the three realms as his home and living beings as his nature. His frame is a withered tree; his samādhi is without contention. The burning house is cold ashes; the toils of dust are a pit of ice. He makes the city his mountain forest and enters right samādhi through speech. So it is no wonder that he is ever speaking, blazing and unceasing, since the sea of wisdom runs across and he cannot himself hold it back. No wonder the master's mouth-gate is never straight.
Praise of Master Lingche
